note: Facebook Pixel keeps everything in one config object, facebook_pixel.settings: facebook_id, visibility.request_path_mode (all_pages|listed_pages), visibility.request_path_pages, visibility.user_role_mode (all_roles|listed_roles), visibility.user_role_roles, and privacy.{donottrack,fb_disable_advanced,eu_cookie_compliance,disable_noscript_img}. The settings form is at /admin/config/facebook_pixel behind the 'configure facebook_pixel' permission. Events are queued through the facebook_pixel.facebook_event service (addEvent/getEvents), which invokes hook_facebook_pixel_event_data_alter($data, $event); the module itself fires ViewContent (node, default/full view mode) and CompleteRegistration (user insert), while PageView comes from js/facebook_pixel.js. Medium cases read the live config; hard cases write real config and, for the second one, require actually coding the alter hook in a module.

evals.prompt: I installed the Drupal facebook_pixel module. Where do I enter my Facebook/Meta Pixel ID in the admin UI, and which config object and key does it end up in?
evals.expected_output: Go to /admin/config/facebook_pixel (route facebook_pixel.facebook_pixel_config_form, permission 'configure facebook_pixel', menu link under Configuration > Web services) and fill in 'Facebook Pixel ID'. It is stored as facebook_id in the facebook_pixel.settings config object, e.g. `drush cset facebook_pixel.settings facebook_id 123456789012345`. If it is empty nothing is tracked at all.

evals.prompt: Using the Drupal facebook_pixel module, how do I fire a custom pixel event such as 'Lead' from my own module's PHP code? Name the service and the method, and explain where the event is stored until it is rendered.
evals.expected_output: Call \Drupal::service('facebook_pixel.facebook_event')->addEvent('Lead', $data) (FacebookEvent::addEvent(string $event, string|array $data = '', bool $start_session = FALSE)). If a session is started - or you pass $start_session TRUE - the event goes into the 'user' private tempstore under the key facebook_pixel; otherwise it goes into a static array for the current request. hook_page_attachments() calls getEvents() and pushes them into drupalSettings.facebook_pixel.events, where js/facebook_pixel.js replays them with fbq('track', …).

evals.prompt: Which hook does the Drupal facebook_pixel module invite modules to implement in order to change the data sent with a pixel event, what is its signature, and which events pass through it?
evals.expected_output: hook_facebook_pixel_event_data_alter(array &$data, $event), documented in facebook_pixel.api.php and invoked with moduleHandler()->invokeAll() at the top of FacebookEvent::addEvent(). Every event queued through the service passes through it - ViewContent, CompleteRegistration and, with the commerce submodule, AddToCart, InitiateCheckout and Purchase. PageView is fired purely in JavaScript and cannot be altered this way.

evals.prompt: Inspect this running Drupal site and report the Facebook Pixel ID that the facebook_pixel module is currently configured with.
evals.expected_output: facebook_pixel.settings has facebook_id: 111222333444555 (readable with `drush cget facebook_pixel.settings facebook_id`).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site the facebook_pixel module has a non-default page rule. Inspect the live configuration and describe on which paths the pixel is added, quoting the exact paths.
evals.expected_output: facebook_pixel.settings has visibility.request_path_mode: listed_pages and visibility.request_path_pages set to "/fbp-eval-landing" and "/fbp-eval-landing/*", so the tracking code is added only on that landing page and anything beneath it.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site please switch on Facebook tracking with our pixel ID 987654321098765, but only track people who are logged in - anonymous visitors must not be tracked. Save the change on the live site.
evals.expected_output: facebook_pixel.settings: facebook_id = '987654321098765', visibility.user_role_mode = 'listed_roles' and visibility.user_role_roles containing 'authenticated' (so only users holding that role are tracked).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create and enable a module at web/modules/custom/facebook_pixel_eval_alter that uses facebook_pixel's event-data alter hook to add the key `fbp_eval_marker` with the value `ok` to the payload of Purchase events only. ViewContent and every other event must be left untouched.
evals.expected_output: An enabled module implements hook_facebook_pixel_event_data_alter(array &$data, $event) and sets $data['fbp_eval_marker'] = 'ok' when $event === 'Purchase'; invoking the hook for ViewContent leaves the payload unchanged.
